containment.rationale: Nothing experimental to contain; even the app's own abstractions (API base, fetching, caching) are centralized in two files, so any future swap is trivial.

justification.rationale: No experimental or very-new APIs are used at all, and the spec (a data-driven Pokédex) genuinely doesn't need any — plain stable Nuxt covers everything.

findings.issue: `setResponseStatus` is imported directly from 'h3', which is not a declared dependency of the app (package.json lists only nuxt, vue, vue-router); it resolves via hoisting.
findings.suggestion: Use Nuxt's auto-imported `setResponseStatus` (exported from #app/composables/ssr, confirmed in app/.nuxt/types/imports.d.ts) so the app doesn't depend on an undeclared transitive package.

findings.issue: Manually reads process.env.API_BASE_URL at runtime and stashes it in useState instead of using Nuxt's standard runtime-config env override (NUXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL).
findings.suggestion: Rely on runtimeConfig's built-in env-var mapping (NUXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL) and drop the manual process.env read, or document why the custom var name is required by the harness.

summary: This app is deliberately conservative: every API it touches — file routing, layouts, useAsyncData, useState, useRuntimeConfig, useHead, useRequestEvent, h3's setResponseStatus — has been stable in Nuxt for a year or more, and nuxt.config.ts enables zero experimental flags. The pinned nuxt ^4.6.3 is the current stable release, including the latest security patches. The only nits are dependency hygiene (importing 'h3' without declaring it) and a manual env-var read that bypasses runtimeConfig conventions — neither is an experimentalness risk.
